# Config reference

Generated by `conductor-docs`. The keys, their types, the rules and the type descriptions are the specification's, [`spec/domains/config.yaml`](https://github.com/beyond10x/conductor/blob/main/spec/domains/config.yaml); each default is what `conductor config show` prints for a file that leaves the key out, read through the same library the binary runs. A key marked required is one whose absence `conductor config validate` refuses. The hand-written [config guide](https://github.com/beyond10x/conductor/blob/main/docs/config.md) says which part of conductor reads each key.

> The one file that names conductor's instances, `conductor.config/1`, read from `--config`, else the `conductor-config` setting, else ~/.b10x/conductor/conductor.yaml. An instance is one organization conductor runs: where its repositories come from, where their checkouts are, where conductor keeps its records, state and cache, which harness and model each role runs on, its cadence, thresholds, reports, and who decides each decision class. These types hold the effective config, after defaults; the file may leave out every key of an instance but its name, its sources and its checkouts. No field takes a secret. What the instances of one file share lives in the host directory, `host/` beside the file (`conductor.host`), not under any instance's `state`.

## Top level

The file. A key it does not declare is an error, and so is a value that looks like a token. `default` is the instance a command runs when neither `--instance` nor the `conductor-instance` setting names one; it names an instance of the file. No two instances share a `session_prefix`, and at most one has none; no two share a `dashboard_port`, so that each instance's dashboard binds its own; no two share a `state` or a `records` directory. The same holds across every config file of the host: `config validate` checks each instance against the host registry (`conductor.host`).

| Key | Type | Default | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | string | required | `version == "conductor.config/1"` |
| `default` | [InstanceName](#instancename) | none | `not defined(default)` or some `instance` in `instances` has `instance.name == default` |
| `instances` | list of [Instance](#instance) | required | `instance.name` distinct across `instances`; `instance.session_prefix` distinct across `instances`; `instance.dashboard_port` distinct across `instances`; `instance.state` distinct across `instances`; `instance.records` distinct across `instances`; `not defined(default)` or some `instance` in `instances` has `instance.name == default` |

## Instance

One instance. A path is written absolute or under `~`, which is the home directory; the effective path is absolute. `operator` is how sessions name the person who decides class O. `session_prefix` is the prefix of every session the instance starts, and of its slice and its dashboard's unit. It is required: `config validate` refuses an instance that writes none, naming the prefix `conductor config migrate` would write (`SuggestedPrefix`). For one release a file without it still loads, so that a running instance keeps working until the operator migrates it: its sessions keep the bare names `conductor`, `conductor-dev` and `<repository>`, its slice `conductor.slice` and its dashboard's unit `conductor-dashboard`. `dashboard_port` is the port on 127.0.0.1 the instance's dashboard serves, 1 to 65535. `conductor` is derived: the conductor that serves the instance. Absent from the file, `records`, `state` and `cache` are ~/.b10x/conductor/&lt;name>/records, ~/.b10x/conductor/&lt;name>/state and ~/.cache/b10x/conductor/&lt;name>, `dashboard_port` is 7313 plus the instance's index in the file (7313 for the first), `repositories` and `reports` are empty, `operator`, `catalog` and `session_prefix` are absent, and every other absent key is conductor's built-in default.

A key path written `a[].b` is the key `b` of each element of the list `a`. A default that holds `<name>` holds the instance's name.

## Types

### InstanceName

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.InstanceName`.

### Harness

The file writes a harness in lower case: `claude` or `codex`.

One of `claude` | `codex`. Specified as `conductor.config.Harness`.

### Tokens

A count of tokens. The file writes a whole number, or thousands with `k`: `300k`.

Written as integer. Specified as `conductor.config.Tokens`.

### Gibibytes

A size in GiB (2^30 bytes). The file writes a whole number with `G`: `15G`.

Written as integer. Specified as `conductor.config.Gibibytes`.

### TimeOfDay

A time of day, UTC, `HH:MM`.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.TimeOfDay`.

### Source

Where an instance's repositories come from. The file writes `{github: <owner>}`, `{local: <path>}` or `{gitlab: <group or root>}`; a `local` or `gitlab` source may add `exclude: [<path under the root>]`, and a `gitlab` source `host: <host name>`.

A repository is the directory that holds `.git` at depth 1 or 2 under a root (`<root>/<repo>` or `<root>/<group>/<repo>`), named by its path under the root (`<group>/<repo>`); the root is a `local` source's path, and for the checkouts of the other sources `checkouts.root`. A repository whose name is an `exclude` entry, or lies under one, is not listed and not placed. Absent, `exclude` is empty. A `github` source takes no `exclude`: GitHub lists its owner's repositories, and the collectors that read that list do not filter it.

One of the forms the keys table lists. Specified as `conductor.config.Source`.

### GitHubSource

An owner on GitHub, whose repositories are the instance's.

Keys: `owner`. Specified as `conductor.config.GitHubSource`.

### LocalSource

A directory whose repositories are the instance's.

Keys: `path`, `exclude`. Specified as `conductor.config.LocalSource`.

### GitLabSource

A group (or the root) on a GitLab forge, whose repositories are the instance's. `host` is the forge's host name, without a scheme or a path, such as `gitlab.example.com` for a self-hosted GitLab; absent, it is `gitlab.com`. The collectors read that forge with `glab api --hostname <host>`: one repository row and one specification row per project of the group and its subgroups, archived ones included, each named by its path under the group. A project's checkout is the git checkout under `checkouts.root` whose `origin` remote is on the host and names the project, read from its git config with no network read.

Keys: `group`, `host`, `exclude`. Specified as `conductor.config.GitLabSource`.

### Checkouts

The directory holding the instance's checkouts, and the one holding their managed worktrees.

Keys: `root`, `trees`. Specified as `conductor.config.Checkouts`.

### CatalogNames

How a catalog entry's file stem spells a repository's name. The file writes it in lower case: `plain`, the name itself, or `hex`, the lower-case hex of the name's UTF-8 bytes.

One of `plain` | `hex`. Specified as `conductor.config.CatalogNames`.

### Catalog

The instance's catalog: `repository` names a repository whose checkout lies under `checkouts.root`, written as its path under the root; `path` is a directory on that repository's `origin/main`, written relative to its top, whose `.json` files name the cataloged repositories, one file each, the name being the file's stem as `names` spells it. Absent, `names` is `plain`. An instance without a catalog records no catalog membership.

Keys: `repository`, `path`, `names`. Specified as `conductor.config.Catalog`.

### CommandWord

A value a start command passes to the harness as one shell word, unquoted: a role's model, agent, settings file or profile file. Letters, digits and `.`, `_`, `:`, `/`, `-` only, so that no shell reads it as more than that word.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.CommandWord`.

### SessionPrefix

The prefix every session one instance starts carries: letters, digits and `-`, starting and ending with a letter or digit. Session names are one namespace for the whole machine, so no two instances of the file share a prefix, no prefix starts with another followed by `-`, which would let one session name carry both, and no prefix followed by `-` begins a name an instance without a prefix keeps, such as `conductor-dev`.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.SessionPrefix`.

### SessionName

A harness session name on this machine: `<session_prefix>-<role or repository>`, or without a prefix the role or the repository itself.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.SessionName`.

### Role

The harness and model one session role runs on, such as `conductor` or `controller`; the harness agent the role starts with, such as `repo-controller`; the settings file it starts with; and the profile file its session starts with through `--append-system-prompt-file`, in place of the agent. The settings and profile files are written absolute or under `~`. Absent, a role names no agent, no settings file and no profile. `session_name` is derived, never chosen: the name the role's session starts under, `<session_prefix>-<role>`, or `<role>` when the instance has no prefix; absent for `controller`, whose sessions are named per repository, `<session_prefix>-<repository>` or `<repository>`. The file may leave it out, and may write only that value. `read_only_tools` names the tools, beyond the guard's built-in read-only allowlist, that the guard allows the role's sessions without a rule of its own, such as a read-only MCP tool; every other tool outside the guard's ruled set is denied. A tool with a rule of its own (Edit, Write, NotebookEdit, SendMessage, Bash, Monitor) is decided by that rule whatever this list says. Absent, it is empty. A `controller` role the file writes that names an `agent` names a `profile` as well: every session of the instance starts with `--setting-sources project,local`, which loads no user-level agent, so a controller starts only from its profile, never from its agent; a controller role with an agent and no profile is refused by its `profile` path. One with neither is valid, as the built-in role is. `limits`, `writable` and `network` are the envelope each session of the role asks for: the limits of one session, the places it may write, and its network; the instance's `confinement` says what happens when the box cannot be set up. A role's limit lies at or under the instance's limit of the same key, where the instance sets one, since every session of the instance runs inside the instance's box. Absent, a role sets no limit, writes its default places, and has the network open. The request leaves out three things on purpose: the readable paths, since the box binds the root read-only and nothing narrower is planned; the programs a session may run, since a program list belongs to the tool server; and a lifetime, since sessions are long-lived and conductor ends them. `forge_token_env` names the environment variables, such as `GH_TOKEN` or `GITLAB_TOKEN`, that carry the forge tokens a session of the role may use: each a name of capital letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit. It is carried on the session request a provider receives (`conductor.session.SessionRequest`); the variables' values are never part of the config. Absent, it is empty. A settings file pins its instance: its `env.CONDUCTOR_INSTANCE` is the instance's name, and each of its hook commands that runs `conductor` names the instance first, `CONDUCTOR_INSTANCE=<name> conductor guard …`, since the harness does not pass the environment its starter set on to a session it forks. A role's own settings file that pins no instance (no `env.CONDUCTOR_INSTANCE`, or a hook command that runs `conductor` without the prefix), as the shipped ones do, starts pinned: `session start` and `spawn` write its content with the pin set to `<state>/sessions/<session name>.settings.json` and start the session with that copy, and `config validate` reports it, by its `settings` path, as a note. A settings file that pins another instance, or cannot be read as JSON, is a problem `config validate` names by its `settings` path, and `session start` and `spawn` refuse it (`InstanceNotPinned`). A role that names none starts with its default written pinned (`conductor.session.SessionStartRefusal`).

Keys: `role`, `harness`, `model`, `agent`, `settings`, `profile`, `session_name`, `read_only_tools`, `limits`, `writable`, `network`, `forge_token_env`. Specified as `conductor.config.Role`.

### Limits

The CPU, memory and process limits of a box, as systemd sets them on a cgroup: `memory_max` its `MemoryMax`, in GiB, written as a size, `15G`; `cpu_weight` its `CPUWeight`, from 1 to 10000; `tasks_max` its `TasksMax`, the most processes and threads at once. Absent, a key sets no limit.

Keys: `memory_max`, `cpu_weight`, `tasks_max`. Specified as `conductor.config.Limits`.

### Writable

One place a role's sessions may write: a path written absolute or under `~`, made absolute, or one of the words for a place resolved per session when it starts: `checkout`, the checkout the session starts in (a controller's repository's, conductor-dev's this repository's); `trees`, the managed worktrees of that checkout under `checkouts.trees`; `build-cache`, the build tools' caches under the home directory (cargo's among them); `scratch`, the session's scratch, under `$TMPDIR` and, for a controller, `<cache>/scratch/<repo>`, under the instance's own `cache` (`<repo>` its repository, `/` written `-`); `harness-state`, the harness's own state directory, `~/.claude` or `~/.codex`; `records`, the instance's records directory. Absent, a role writes `checkout`, `trees`, `build-cache`, `scratch` and `harness-state`, and the `conductor` role `records` as well; a list the file writes takes their place.

Written as string. Specified as `conductor.config.Writable`.

### Network

A session's network. The file writes it in lower case: `open`, the host's network, the only one there is.

One of `open`. Specified as `conductor.config.Network`.

### ConfinementMode

What happens when a session's box cannot be set up. The file writes it in lower case: `strict`, the session does not start; `report`, it starts unboxed, and the reason is recorded.

One of `strict` | `report`. Specified as `conductor.config.ConfinementMode`.

### ConfinementProvider

What sets up a session's box. The file writes it in lower case: `systemd`, a `systemd-run --user` unit per session under the instance's slice; `none`, a host with no provider, which `strict` refuses to start any session on and `report` starts every session on unboxed.

One of `systemd` | `none`. Specified as `conductor.config.ConfinementProvider`.

### RepoCache

Whether `conductor build run` gives a cargo-based command its repository's compile cache. The file writes it in lower case: `on` or `off`.

One of `on` | `off`. Specified as `conductor.config.RepoCache`.

### Confinement

How the instance's sessions are boxed: the `mode`, the `provider`, and the `limits` of the instance as a whole, the slice every session of the instance runs in. They take over the `instances[].limits` an earlier plan named. Absent, the mode is `report`, the provider `systemd`, and no limit is set.

Keys: `mode`, `provider`, `limits`. Specified as `conductor.config.Confinement`.

### ConductorSession

The conductor a session of the instance messages: its own, `session_name` being `<session_prefix>-conductor` or `conductor`, when the instance names a `conductor` role; else the conductor of the file's `default` instance, which serves it, `served_by` naming that instance; neither when no conductor serves it. Derived, never chosen: a file may leave it out, and may write only that value.

Keys: `served_by`, `session_name`. Specified as `conductor.config.ConductorSession`.

### Controllers

How many controllers of the instance work at once, at most, how many sub-agents one controller runs at once, at most, and how many pull requests of one repository may wait for review before conductor sends that repository no new dispatch, `0` meaning no limit. Absent, they are 5, 4 and 3.

Keys: `max_working`, `max_subagents`, `max_open_reviews`. Specified as `conductor.config.Controllers`.

### RepositoryRule

The activity of the repositories whose name `match` names. The file writes an activity in lower case: `active` or `inactive`.

Keys: `match`, `activity`. Specified as `conductor.config.RepositoryRule`.

### Cadence

How often conductor runs a cycle, when its daily cycle starts, and how often the watch reads the sessions and main's CI. The file writes a duration as a whole number with `s`, `m`, `h` or `d`: `2h`, `180s`.

Keys: `cycle`, `daily`, `watch`, `ci`. Specified as `conductor.config.Cadence`.

### Thresholds

Conductor's context above which it hands over; the filesystem whose free space the disk thresholds read, written absolute or under `~`; free disk under which the watch reports it, from which a further fall is reported again, under which no session starts, and under which a full gate takes a build slot; the size above which a build is expected to write enough to ask for a slot; free disk under which the full-gate watchdog stops the gate's process group and from which it resumes it; how often the watchdog reads it; and how long a live controller session, and every one of its sub-agents, may write nothing to its transcript before the watch reports it silent, a duration as `cadence` writes one; and how many CPU cores `conductor build run` leaves to the desktop: its command's job count is the cores less this; and how many `conductor build run` commands run at once on the host, every instance's together: a request is granted only while fewer disk grants than this are `Granted` or `Running`, waits in the queue's order while they are not, and is never refused for it, 0 for no bound; whether `build run` gives a cargo-based command its repository's compile cache, one sccache server and directory per repository that all of its worktrees share, and that cache's size; and the short lane: how many build slots besides `build_slots` admit only a command the ledger knows to be short, 0 turning the lane off, and the longest p90 run time of such a command, a duration as `cadence` writes one. A request is short when the ledger holds at least 3 earlier runs of its repository and command in 14 days whose p90 run time is at most `short_lane_max`, and no short-lane run of it outlived twice that in the last 24 hours. Absent, the filesystem is `/`, the silence 30 minutes, the reserve 2 cores, the build slots 3, the repository cache `on` and its size 2G, the short-lane slots 1 and their longest p90 3 minutes.

Keys: `context_handover`, `disk_path`, `disk_low`, `disk_clear`, `disk_admit`, `build_slot`, `build_size`, `gate_stop`, `gate_resume`, `watchdog_every`, `silent_session`, `cpu_reserve`, `build_slots`, `repo_cache`, `repo_cache_size`, `short_lane_slots`, `short_lane_max`. Specified as `conductor.config.Thresholds`.

### Retention

How many snapshots' observations the instance keeps: those of the newest `snapshots` complete ones. Absent, it is 12, a day at the 2-hour cadence.

Keys: `snapshots`. Specified as `conductor.config.Retention`.

### Report

Where a report goes, as whom it is posted, and on which occasions.

Keys: `channel`, `as`, `when`. Specified as `conductor.config.Report`.

### Authority

Who decides a class-C and a class-O decision. The file writes `conductor` or `operator`.

Keys: `class_c`, `class_o`. Specified as `conductor.config.Authority`.

### SecretSync

One secret sync of the instance: a file on a branch of one of its repositories that the organization's own tool publishes into GitHub Actions secrets, which its CI reads. `name` names the sync on the board; `source` is the file; `secrets` are the secrets it feeds, one or more; `command` is the command line that publishes it, and `dry_run`, when given, the one that shows what `command` would publish without publishing it. Conductor runs neither: the snapshot reads the source's last commit and each secret's `updated_at`, and the board flags `secret stale: <name>` when the source changed after a secret was written. The conductor session runs `command` only where the instance's `rules.md` grants it. No two syncs of an instance share a name.

Keys: `name`, `source`, `secrets`, `command`, `dry_run`. Specified as `conductor.config.SecretSync`.

### SecretSource

The file a secret sync publishes: `repository` names a repository whose checkout lies under `checkouts.root`, written as its path under the root; `path` is the file, written relative to that repository's top; `branch` is the branch its last commit is read on, as `origin/<branch>`, `main` when absent. Neither path takes `.` or `..` steps.

Keys: `repository`, `branch`, `path`. Specified as `conductor.config.SecretSource`.

### ForgeSecret

One GitHub Actions secret a sync feeds, by its `name`: the organization `owner`'s secret, or, when `repository` is given, that repository's of the owner. It is read with `gh api` (`GET /orgs/<owner>/actions/secrets/<name>`, `GET /repos/<owner>/<repository>/actions/secrets/ <name>`), which answers the secret's `updated_at` and never its value.

Keys: `owner`, `repository`, `name`. Specified as `conductor.config.ForgeSecret`.

### Usage

How the instance reads its harness accounts' usage. `probe` is a command, run with `sh -c` on each snapshot, that prints the accounts as one JSON object: `accounts`, a list, each with `id` (the account; conductor keeps nothing else of it, never an e-mail address or a name), `active` (whether it is the account in use), `health` (`exhausted` for one with nothing left) and `usage.windows`, a list of `{name, used_percent, resets_at}`; every other key is ignored. `watcher` is the systemd user unit that rotates the accounts, which `conductor doctor` reports running or not. Conductor names no tool: both are the operator's. Absent, neither is set: no probe runs and doctor reports no watcher.

Keys: `probe`, `watcher`. Specified as `conductor.config.Usage`.

### Activity

One of `active` | `inactive`. Specified as `conductor.direction.Activity`.

### Decider

One of `conductor` | `operator`. Specified as `conductor.decision.Decider`.
